description: Use for a synthetic commerce order with a late, missing, failed, or return-related fulfillment signal that needs policy-grounded recovery, governed execution, verification, and notification.
planning_instructions: Read get_order_context and list_fulfillment_options first. Treat their current order version and bounded option IDs as authoritative.
When the request supplies an operator-constrained option ID, evaluate only that option. Do not substitute a different recovery after a denied, insufficient-evidence, or conflicting-evidence result.

Search the domain knowledge gateway with the order tenant, jurisdiction, event decision_time, and the channel to which the requested option's governing evidence applies. Scope by the decision being made, not by incidental words in the trigger: use the order interaction channel from get_order_context for same-sku-replacement, refund-merchandise, cancel-and-refund, and wait-for-current-fulfillment; use shipping only for carrier-service-claim. For a replacement query, seek enterprise replacement authorization, inventory/risk bounds, restrictions, and approval thresholds; do not substitute carrier postage-refund rules. Sections marked all or global remain eligible in either search. Omit optional tags during initial discovery unless their controlled values came from a prior gateway result; if used, tags are OR-match filters. Use the identical chosen scope and time for every exact decisive-section read; keep each evidence_receipt with its section ID, release ID, and content hash.

Use relation traversal when a retrieved section points to an exception, prerequisite, authority, implementing procedure, or conflict. A narrower applicable exception overrides a general section. When equally applicable sections are connected by CONFLICTS_WITH and no reviewed precedence relation resolves them, exact-read and cite both so the deterministic evaluator can classify conflicting_evidence.

Pass the shared decision_time, paired retrieved exact section IDs and signed evidence receipts, release ID, and release hash to evaluate_recovery_policy. Call it even when scoped order facts appear incomplete; it owns the auditable terminal classification. Never leave a documented required parameter empty: bind order_id from get_order_context and option_id from the operator constraint. Once the decisive section IDs are known, place their exact reads and evaluate_recovery_policy in the same continuation phase by making evaluation depend directly on every exact-read step and referencing their receipts. If evaluation is the last step in a phase, set terminal=false so the next phase can branch on its actual deterministic outcome.
Never execute an ineligible decision. Use the returned decision_token and a stable idempotency key composed from order ID, option ID, and evaluated order version.

For allowed, call execute_recovery_command with the returned token and stable idempotency key. For approval_required, also call execute_recovery_command with the token and idempotency key but omit approval_reference and approval_proof: the framework intercepts that sensitive step and creates the HITL checkpoint before HTTP dispatch. An approval_required evaluation is not itself a checkpoint and must not be reported as pending approval unless execution was interrupted. Never fabricate approval_reference or approval_proof; the runtime injects them only after checkpoint approval. The execution phase must never contain execute alone: in that same plan, add verify_order_outcome depending directly on execute, then send_synthetic_notification depending directly on both execute and verify. Every step that references another step's output must name that source step directly in depends_on, even when another dependency already provides a transitive path. This full downstream chain is persisted in the HITL checkpoint and resumes together. Do not claim completion unless verification returned verified=true.

Treat evaluate_recovery_policy.outcome as authoritative. For denied, insufficient_evidence, or conflicting_evidence, do not call execute_recovery_command; abstain and report the exact outcome and reasons. If evidence is missing, conflicting, stale, or filtered out, never invent policy.
response_instructions: Report observed order state, exact evidence section IDs with source URLs and release hash, deterministic policy outcome and reasons, approval status, command reference, verification, and notification reference.
Do not describe a pending approval, transport success, or unverified state as a completed recovery.
tool_hints: Use commerce-core for order state, options, deterministic evaluation, execution, verification, and synthetic notification.
Use domain-knowledge-gateway for hybrid search, relation traversal, exact reads, and release provenance.

should_activate: Recover order ORD-1003 after a missing in transit signal
Determine whether a day-35 electronics return is eligible
Handle a missed promised ship date without customer consent

change_reason: Require scoped exact-read receipts, runtime approval proof, deterministic revalidation, and action-specific verification
